newsitem.title: UK: N Sea crude premiums firm but ready to head lower.
newsitem.headline: N Sea crude premiums firm but ready to head lower.

text.p: North Sea crudes traded on Tuesday at firmer differentials as buyers emerged for second half June barrels against a background of a falling outright price, but traders said the grades had reached their peak and should come off in a well supplied market.
July Brent on IPE futures lost some 75 cents by 1715 GMT to $19.25 a barrel. On the Brent CFD market the current week was supported by buying at strong levels of physical Brent by one trader.
The week (May 27-30) was last heard offered at July -1 cent. Further forward the weakness in the market was more apparent.
The following three weeks were offered at July -20 cents and bids five cents lower.

On the physical market a refiner picked up two second decade June Ekofisk cargoes at a 20 cent premium to dated Brent. This compared to an early June deal at the end of last week at dated Brent +10 cents.
A cargo of June 8-10 Statfjord sold at dated Brent +35 cents, up four cents from last done.
Refiners said outright levels would have to fall further and saw the grades coming off in the next week or so as margins continued to look poor and the crude market oversupplied.
"I think we will be weaker on the wet grades. The (refining) margins just wont sustain these levels and there is far too much crude around," one U.K. based refiner said.
Intermonth spreads lost ground with the fall on outright prices. The July/Aug talked at -13/-10 cents while Aug/Sept was -6/-3 cents.
In the Mediterranean, Russian Urals looked to have climbed slightly off recent lows of under Dated Brent -$1.40 cents, although poor margins kept the lid on differentials.
One seller of a large May-loading Urals cargo said this morning that it was on offer at Dated Brent -$1.35/-$1.30.
